claims.statement: In REDEFINE 1, a phase 3, 68-week, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled trial in 3,417 adults with overweight/obesity (without type 2 diabetes), cagrilintide 2.4 mg once weekly as monotherapy produced an average body weight reduction of 11.8% versus 2.3% with placebo, with 31.6% of cagrilintide recipients achieving greater than 15% weight loss versus 4.7% on placebo; the most common adverse effects were mild-to-moderate gastrointestinal events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation), and the regimen was reported as well tolerated in this trial population.

context.doseText: Trial protocol dose: cagrilintide 2.4 mg once weekly after titration, monotherapy arm of REDEFINE 1, 68 weeks (trial protocol description; not a use recommendation)

claims.statement: Coadministered with semaglutide as CagriSema (2.4 mg/2.4 mg once weekly) in REDEFINE 1 (adults with overweight/obesity, no type 2 diabetes), weight loss at week 68 was -20.4% versus -3.0% with placebo (estimated difference -17.3 percentage points, p<0.001), exceeding either monotherapy arm; in REDEFINE 2 (adults with overweight/obesity and type 2 diabetes), CagriSema produced -13.7% weight loss versus -3.4% with placebo (estimated difference -10.4 percentage points, p<0.001), and 74% of REDEFINE 2 participants receiving CagriSema achieved HbA1c ≤6.5% versus 15.9% with placebo. Gastrointestinal adverse events were substantially more frequent with CagriSema than placebo (80% vs 40% in REDEFINE 1).

claims.statement: Gray-market vendor and content pages marketing research-grade cagrilintide describe benefits in broader, more definitive terms than the controlled trial record supports — including claims of 'near-complete appetite loss' in some users, weight loss framed as being 'predominantly from fat mass, with preserved lean mass,' and self-administration titration schedules (e.g., weekly dose escalation from 0.16 mg to a 2.4 mg maintenance dose) presented as established protocol — despite cagrilintide having no FDA-approved product, no approved dosing regimen, and only trial-controlled (not self-administered, unsupervised) human safety data. Body-composition (fat-vs-lean mass) effects and the extremes of appetite suppression described on these pages are not supported by the extracted trial-summary evidence in this packet, which reports only mean weight-loss percentages and standard GI adverse-event rates.
